Subject: Partnership: evidence custody & escrow workflow

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this call last week. Sentinel Allies supports several ISVs with GRC integrations; our customers frequently ask for a standard way to exchange SOC2 artifacts and timeboxed pen-test evidence without exposing raw logs or persistent access. We put together a short draft of an "evidence custody playbook" that outlines roles, TTLs, storage, and transfer options (attached).

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood accept time-limited evidence bundles via a partner escrow flow (S3 presigned + short-lived access) or via an encrypted artifact gateway?
- What metadata schema do you need for each artifact (control ID, test window, hash, retention policy)?
- Do you require a legal addendum for evidence-handling (NDA + limited-use clause) before we ship artifacts?

We can coordinate an ops + legal sync if helpful. Attached: evidence-handoff-matrix.xlsx (working draft).

Best,
Ana Costa
Head of Integrations, Sentinel Allies

Ana — thanks for the clear draft and for outlining the options. Short answers up front: we can support both presigned S3 bundles and an encrypted artifact gateway; each has different operational and legal footprints.

Quick notes:
- Metadata: we need control ID, evidence type, test window (UTC start/stop), artifact checksum (SHA256), and source system tag. TTLs we typically enforce are 30 days for pen-test evidence and 90 days for attestation artifacts, but we can make them configurable per-partner.
- Legal: we usually pair an evidence-handling addendum with the partner SOW; happy to start with Sentinel's wording and iterate.

I'll loop in Karthik for the technical details and Monica for contracting. Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to confirm S3 presigned upload presets and Gateway encryption options.
2) Monica to flag any procurement or legal gating items.
3) Ana to confirm which of your customers we pilot with and proposed retention TTLs.

Can we aim for a short working session next Tue (6/8) at 11am PT?

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hey team — quick note from Cobalt's ops side. We reviewed the matrix and added a short PDF with redlines (attached). Two items to call out:
- We prefer not to use long-lived presigned URLs for upload; accept short-lived presigned + multipart upload window to avoid accidental exposure.
- Proof-of-custody: include an HMAC signature on the artifact manifest (in addition to SHA256). That lets downstream consumers validate the sender.

We're happy to participate in the Tuesday 6/8 working session. Also attaching a sample set of artifact metadata we use with several GRC vendors.

— Matt Reynolds
